answer: A basalt foundation audit makes each newcomer build proof that cannot be faked. They lock a $140 bond and register one key, then lay four basalt courses over 28 days, photographing each at dawn with a walnut shell token in frame. Three established peers inspect every course within 48 hours, and two failed inspections burn the bond plus a 60-day wait. Forging 1,000 identities needs $140,000, 4,000 photographed courses, and about 8,000 hours of real labor. A walnut shell in the photo is small, but it proves a human stood there at dawn, the way a foundation stone proves a house will stand.
